title: Mt. Zion preparing for conference rival Mahomet-Seymour - NewsBreak
text:
By Tristan Thomas ,
2 hours ago
MT. ZION, Ill. (WCIA) -- After last season's Mahomet-Seymour and Mt. Zion game ended up being the difference in deciding an Apollo Conference Champion, the Braves are eager to play the Bulldogs on home turf.
"You love playing them," senior quarterback and safety Connor Fox said. "It's a game that we circle, but it's not a game that we make too much of it." "It's another game, but it is a big game, and we know that."
"Even the community is looking forward to this game, we can't put too much work into it and not look at the other games that we have this year, but you definitely get the adrenaline going as soon as you walk on that field and you see Mahomet over there," senior running back Kellen Bollhorst said.
This year Mt. Zion brings a much different roster into the rivalry after replacing 25 seniors, with head coach Patrick Etherton setting the focus on consistent progression.
"We want to play our best football at the end of the season; we don't want to play it now," Etherton said. "We want to make sure that we continue to get better as coaches, get our kids in the right positions, figure out what we can and cannot do."
The quarterback position is a key part of that. Fox and junior Noah Schmal have split reps this season.
"They've both made plays in different things that we've asked them to do, and we'll continue to look at it," Etherton said.
"We learn what we do best and we can apply it to each other's games and learn off of each other, and I think we've both gotten better through it," Fox said. "We see different things, we do different things, and I think it keeps other teams on edge of what we might do."
Moving the chains and winning the turnover battle are among Mt Zion's key to victory in our Friday Football Fever Spotlight Game of the Week.
That could be a challenge against an undefeated Mahomet-Seymour squad that's won each of its last three games by at least 34 points.
